notes: Arizona is the fullest ladder in the namespace so far: one page of the Corporations Division FAQ prices regular processing, an ordinary $35 expedite and a three-step Same Day/Next Day service ($100 / $200 / $400) in a single list, each with the time it buys. Every one of the four is stated as an addition to the filing fee, so the numbers here are surcharges, not totals. The LLC fee schedule (Rev. 3.2026) prints the same thing the other way round, as totals: Articles of Organization $50.00 for regular processing and $85.00 for expedited processing, which is where appliesToLlcFormation comes from - the expedite column is priced for the LLC formation document itself, not for corporations by reference. Day ranges are deliberately not parsed into the business-day fields: the agency says 'days' and defines processing time as 'the estimated number of days it will take for our staff to review your filing', so reading 14-16 or 3-5 as business days would add a qualifier the page does not carry. What the accelerated tiers buy is examination, not acceptance: 'The accelerated service guarantees the examination of a document within the specified service time' and 'Same day/next day filing does not guarantee approval of a filing' - the North Carolina shape. chargedIfRejected is true on the strength of the division's own payment page, which states that all filing fees are NONREFUNDABLE pursuant to A.R.S. 10-122, 10-3122 and 29-3213; the softer half is that a rejected document, when resubmitted, is processed under the accelerated service originally paid for unless a faster one is bought. Two more conditions worth carrying: the accelerated clock starts only when the document is complete and paid for, and does not start until a required statutory agent acceptance has been accepted, which for an online formation means manually accepting the electronic version from the dashboard. Mailed documents, FedEx included, are not accepted for Same Day/Next Day at all.
needsReview: Standard processing time is the FAQ's estimate, not the live figure. The division's current processing times are published at arizonabusinesscenter.azcc.gov/processingTimes, which returned HTTP 403 on this route; the routing plan measured that host as reachable only with the VPN down, so it is a route-dependent read rather than a dead page and should be taken on the other route or in a browser.
